2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 23.03.2021, deceased Smt.

Rajeshwari Paraddi and her relatives were traveling in a new Bolero Jeep so as to go to Dharmasthala and Kukke Subramanya, when the said Bolero Jeep was NC: 2025:KHC-K:6567-DB HC-KAR proceeding at last curving of Arebali Ghat, at 12.40 p.m. at Arebali Yellapur in Uttarkannada District, at the distance of 18 k.m. from Yellapur P.S., at that time, a lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-22/B-9755 had parked dangerously obstructing the way to the vehicles and so also without switching on the indicators.
Therefore, the driver of the said Bolero Jeep has slow down the Jeep so as to move towards right side of the lorry.

At that time, another Lorry bearing Hanamanth And Ors vs Revanna A P And Ors on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88584878/
3 No.KA-13/C-4468, came from behind the said jeep by driving the same in very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed heavily to the Jeep and dragged the Jeep towards front side.

sentences.text: At that time, a Tipper bearing No.KA-17/7640 came from the opposite direction.
Therefore, the Bolero Jeep caught between the Lorry No.KA-13/C-4468 and the said Tipper and crushed.
3. In the said accident, deceased Rajeshwari sustained fatal injuries towards her head and face and died on the spot and another occupant also died in the said accident.

NC: 2025:KHC-K:6567-DB HC-KAR 4. Deceased - Rajeshwari was hale and healthy and was doing agriculture, tailoring and also doing household work and out of the said avocation she was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The petitioners were entirely depended upon the income.
Hence, the claimants filed the claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act before the Claims Tribunal seeking compensation for the death of deceased Rajeshwari.
5. Though notice was duly served, respondent Nos.1 and 3 remained absent, hence they were placed ex parte.
The respondent No. 4 - the insurance company represented by its counsel and filed its written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
6. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimants, in order to prove the case, claimant No.1 got examined herself as PW-1 and got exhibited documents namely, Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.

On behalf of NC:
2025:KHC-K:6567-DB HC-KAR respondents, two witnesses have been examined as R.W.1 and 2 and got marked two documents as Exs.R.1 and 2.
7.

The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment inter alia held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the drivers of both the Lorries, as a result of which,
deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal, upon considering the oral and documentary evidence placed before it, held that the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.23,00,400/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed respondent Nos.2 and 4, the insurance companies to deposit 50% each of the compensation amount.
Being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation, this appeal has been filed.

8. The learned counsel for the claimants raised the following contentions:
a) At the time of accident, deceased was aged about 32 years and she was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. NC: 2025:KHC-K:6567-DB HC-KAR
However, the Tribunal has assessed notional income of deceased at Rs.12,000/-, which is on the lower side.

b) Lastly, contended that in view of judgment of Apex Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -V- NANU RAM [2018 ACJ 2782], the claimant No.1 is entitled for Rs.44,000/- under the head 'loss of spousal consortium' and claimant Nos.2 and 3 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head 'loss of Hanamanth And Ors vs Revanna A P And Ors on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88584878/
4 parental consortium'.
9.

Hence, on these grounds sought for dismissal of the appeal.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6567-DB HC-KAR 11.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties, perused the judgment and award including the appeal papers.

12. It is not in dispute that deceased Smt. Rajeshwari died in a road traffic accident occurred on 23.03.2021 due to the rash and negligence of driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-22/B-9755 and the lorry bearing Registration No.KA-13/C-4468.
Even though the claimants claimed monthly income of deceased at Rs.30,000/-, they have not produced any document to establish the same.

Under these circumstances, the notional income of deceased Rs.14,250/- p.m. has to be considered as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident occurring in 2021.
The age of deceased was 32 years at the time of accident.
The Tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier of '16' and rightly deducted 1/3rd income of deceased towards his personal expenses.
Accordingly, the 'loss of dependency' has been re-

14. Thus, on re-assessing the compensation, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation:

ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.
